mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% quarter-over-quarter signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and lowers earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.
